display_name: Procopius of Jerusalem, son of Theodosia

names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 8 iulie, «Sfântul Mare Mucenic Procopie», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Προκόπιος ο Μεγαλομάρτυς», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 8. јул ст. ст., „Св. вел. муч. Прокопије“ — Св. is not a rank and „вел. муч.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the bare forename is left, which is all this heading gives. «of Jerusalem, son of Theodosia» in the display name is the corpus’s own disambiguation off two other books, and „Неаније“, the name he bore before the Lord baptised him in the prison, is **not** written as a second form: §6 wants one form per folder, and the folder already carries that name in its older prose. **The fold is forced and it is shared with this same day’s other entry**: `foldchk.py` returns `procopius-of-sazava`, `sr`, for this string, and `procopius-of-ustyug` takes the same form from the day’s second heading, so three folders hold it after this day.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 1844, with the rank word after the last comma left off. The parenthesis is the page’s own and is kept whole: it records the name Neanias he bore before his martyrdom, which is a reading and not a rank. `fk.mjs` returns no other holder.

death.note: doxologia.ro sets the whole story under «Dioclețian, păgânul împărat al Romei» and dates only the day: «și-a pus sufletul pentru Domnul său, în 8 zile ale lunii lui iulie». The interval is Diocletian's reign; the page gives no year.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 июля ст. ст. — «Вмч. Прокопия (303).»

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, and this folder’s man: the same menologion day its Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows already keep, the same rank of great-martyr. Name page 1844 heads him «Прокопий (до мученичества Неаний) Кесарийский (Палестинский), вмч.» — Procopius, called Neanias before his martyrdom, of Caesarea in Palestine — which is the same man this folder keeps as the son of Theodosia; `theodosia-mother-of-procopius` is NOT named on this day page and its undocumented russian row was not touched. THE READING life4181 WAS NOT OPENED; this row rests on the day line, the name page and the two hymns. `dates` UNCHANGED, and the line is the first source read to give a year: «(303)», where the folder carries «under Diocletian» off doxologia.ro, which dated only the day. 303 lies inside that reign, so nothing held is contradicted; whether the folder should take the flat year is an author question in the report. The epithet differs from the folder’s own display name — this calendar says Caesarea in Palestine where the corpus’s slug and display say Jerusalem — and nothing was renamed on it. Two hymns taken. The troparion is the common of a martyr with his name set into it, «Мученик Твой, Господи, Прокопий», which is his service and is copied whole; the kontakion is proper to him. THREE DIFFERENT PROCOPII STAND ON THIS ONE DAY and the corpus already held all three: the great-martyr of Caesarea in Palestine (303), the fool-for-Christ of Veliky Ustyug (1303) and the righteous one of Usya (XVII). Each has a name page of its own — 1844, 1847, 1846 — each listing «День памяти: 8 июля» and no other day, and the hymn headings on the day page keep them apart by the same epithets. No row was written on a bare forename anywhere here. THE DAY IS MOSTLY ICONS AND ALL OF THEM ARE LEFT OUT: the appearing of the Kazan icon at Kazan in 1579, the sign from the Annunciation icon at Ustyug in 1290, the Jacobstadt icon, and one line that lists FIFTEEN honoured copies of the Kazan icon by city and year with a name link and a reading behind each. Five of the day’s eight entries are that, and none of them is a folder; their hymns — two for the Kazan icon with a величание, one for the Tambov copy and one for the Ustyug Annunciation — were not copied.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 8 iulie — «Sfântul Mare Mucenic Procopie»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Προκόπιος ο Μεγαλομάρτυς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and gives the same man: raised at Jerusalem under Diocletian, son of the devout Christopher and of the idolatrous Theodosia, whom the folder already keeps beside him. It heads him «(; - 303)». The same day's listing carries three further men of the name — the fool for Christ of Ustyug, the saint of Usya in Vologda, and «Άγιος Προκόπιος ο εφορκιστής», which carries the site's own asterisk and says in its own words that he is «άλλος συνώνυμος του μεγαλομάρτυρα Προκοπίου»; that one is refused and the first two are drafted as new folders. The page prints hymns, but the extractor cut it in the middle and no hymn was read whole, so none is taken.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.07.2026 (8. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. вел. муч. Прокопије“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 8 July is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated row or rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **THE NARROWING REFUSAL, FOR THE FOURTH FOLDER IN TWO DAYS, AND THE LINE IT DRAWS.** `procopius-of-jerusalem` holds `death` 284 to 305, display «under Diocletian», off doxologia, which «sets the whole story under Dioclețian … and dates only the day» and gives no year. This book ends „Чесно пострада св. Прокопије у Кесарији Палестинској и увенча се венцем бесмртне славе 8. јула 303 год.“ — a **stated day and year**, 8 July 303, at Caesarea in Palestine. 303 lies inside 284 to 305, so there is nothing to widen; and writing it would replace a recorded interval with a point. **Refused, on the same ground as Kyriake’s 289 and the two monks’ «about 290» yesterday**, and the line this range has in fact been drawing is worth stating once: **a stated year fills an empty field and does not displace a recorded interval.** That is why Hyacinth’s 108 went in flat on 3 July against saint.gr’s reign of Trajan — the field was `null` and the reign was never in it — and why these four do not. `dates` is passed back verbatim, note and all; the day and the year and the city go into the life; **and the alternative is one edit per folder**, here `death` 303 to 303, display «303», basis traditional. `twelve-women-senators` holds `death` 303 off saint.gr’s page head, which **is not used here**: a folder’s date is not widened or set on another folder’s prose. WHAT IS NEW, AND THREE OF IT ARE WORTH THE LIFE. **The road to Alexandria told as Saul’s road.** The folder had the vision; this book says outright that „деси се Неанију нешто слично као негда и Савлу“, something happened to Neanias like what once happened to Saul, and gives the hour — the third hour of the night — the earthquake, the question „Неаније, камо идеш, и на кога устајеш?“, his own „Ко си ти, Господе? Не могу да те познам“, the cross shown in the air as if of crystal, and the words from it, „Ја сам Исус распети Син Божји“, with the charge „Овим знамењем које си видео побеђуј непријатеље своје, и мир мој биће с тобом“. **The campaign he made instead of the one he was sent on.** He had such a cross made as he had seen, and instead of marching against the Christians he marched with his army against the Agarenes who were striking at Jerusalem, and entered the city as victor, and told his mother he was a Christian — none of which is in the folder. The unbuckling of the commander’s belt and sword and the throwing of them before the judge, to show that he was only a soldier of Christ the King. The second appearing, in prison, where **the Lord baptised him himself and gave him the name Procopius**. **AND A LITURGICAL FACT NEITHER OTHER BOOK HAS.** „Зато се у чину венчања брачних помиње св. Прокопије, поред боговенчаног цара Константина и Јелене“ — for that reason he is commemorated in the rite of marriage, beside the God-crowned emperor Constantine and Helen. It is written into the life because it is a fact about the Church’s own service and not about a kinship, and **Constantine and Helen take no row**: `constantine-the-great` and the Helen of that pair are named in a liturgical remark, which is not a relation any more than sharing a day is. The end is new too: at the place of execution he raised his hands to the east and prayed for all the poor and afflicted, the orphaned and the widowed, and especially for the holy Church, that it might grow and spread and that Orthodoxy might shine to the end of time; and it was made known to him from heaven that his prayer was heard, after which he laid his head gladly under the sword. `types` UNTOUCHED: `great-martyr` and `soldier` are both there; „вел. муч.“ is the `great-martyr` and the military service the `soldier`, and both are already held, so the 5 and 7 July case of a heading’s rank having to be written does not recur. No `office`: a commander’s belt is not a see, and he threw it down. No `locations`: Jerusalem, Alexandria and Caesarea in Palestine in a narrative are not coordinates, and this folder’s dates read as a twenty-one-year interval. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder already relates `theodosia-mother-of-procopius`. **THE TWELVE WOMEN AND THE MOTHER GET NO ROW, AND ONE OF THE TWO FOLDERS IS KEPT ON THIS VERY NUMBER.** The body has twelve women come to the prison window and say „И ми смо слушкиње Христове“, and we too are Christ’s handmaids; they were thrown into the same prison, where Procopius taught them the faith and especially how to receive the martyr’s crown; they were then fearfully tortured, and watching their torments **his own mother also believed, so that all thirteen were put to death**. `twelve-women-senators` is a folder, `martyr`, kept **venerated by the Greek calendar on the Julian 8 July — the same number this row is written on** — and already related by this folder in the Greek wave’s reading; `theodosia-mother-of-procopius` is a folder too, `martyr`, kept venerated by the Romanian and Greek calendars on the same 8 July, and **already related in both directions**. Neither takes a `serbian` row. The heading is „Св. вел. муч. Прокопије“ and §4 is explicit that a row’s quoted line is the heading, whole, while §5 says the count is what the heading enumerates. **This is the fourth day running** on which a folder standing on the day’s own number has been refused a row for want of a place in the heading — the six monks on 5 July, Audifax and Abachum on 6 July, the bishop of Tomis on 7 July. **And the mother is not even named here**: this book says only „мајка Прокопијева“, so her row would have been a narrated martyrdom with no name, which gets no row twice over. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE DAY’S TWO PROCOPII FOLD ONTO EACH OTHER, AND THAT IS MEASURED AND FORCED.** Entry 1 is „Св. вел. муч. Прокопије“ and entry 2 is „Св. Прокопије Јуродиви“. Свети is not a rank; „вел. муч.“ is the great-martyr; and **„Јуродиви“ is a rank too** — §5 lists Христа ради јуродиви / Јуродиви as `fool-for-christ`, which is a `types` word and not a by-name. So both headings reduce to the bare «Прокопије», and the two folders this day writes take the same `sr` form. `foldchk.py` returns `procopius-of-sazava`, `sr`, for that string, so after this day **three folders hold it**, two of them written on one day. **This is the 18 June case with the answer going the other way**: there both entries were a Leontius and keeping „прозорљиви“ was the only reason the day’s two folders did not fold together — but that word is a by-name with no `types` behind it, where „Јуродиви“ is the rank the folder already carries. A rank may not be kept in a form to break a fold. «Прокопије Јуродиви» was measured and holds nobody, and was refused on the rule; „Устјужски“, which would also have broken it, stands in the **body** and a by-name is kept only where the heading itself gives one. The three are told apart by their display names, their `types` and their days: a `great-martyr` and `soldier` of Caesarea on 8 July, a `fool-for-christ` and `wonderworker` of Ustyug on 8 July, and the Bohemian abbot of Sázava.

hymns.text: Nu de la oameni, ci de la Dumnezeu primind chemare, sfinte, ai lăsat credinţa părintească cea rea şi slujbele cele orânduite; şi râvnind după Hristos, ca un al doilea Pavel, ai suferit multe osteneli şi răni. Şi primind acum cununa cea făgăduită, Mare Mucenice Procopie, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Mare Mucenic Procopie», Glasul 8

english.text: Receiving your calling not from men but from God, holy one, you left the bad faith of your fathers and the appointed services; and in zeal for Christ, like a second Paul, you endured many labours and wounds. Having now received the promised crown, Procopius, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Мученик Твой, Господи, Прокопий/ во страдании своем венец прият нетленный от Тебе, Бога нашего:/ имели бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложи,/ сокруши и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Того молитвами/ спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 июля ст. ст. — «Тропарь великомученика Прокопия», глас 4

english.text: Thy martyr Procopius, O Lord, in his contest received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength he cast down the tormentors and broke the feeble insolence of the demons. By his prayers save our souls.

hymns.text: Ревностию ко Христу Божественною распалаемь/ и Креста крепостию ограждаемь,/ врагов шатание и дерзость низложил еси, Прокопие,/ и честную Церковь возвысил еси,/ верою преуспевая и просвещая нас.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 июля ст. ст. — «Кондак великомученика Прокопия», глас 2

english.text: Set alight with divine zeal for Christ and walled about with the strength of the Cross, thou didst cast down the raging and the insolence of the enemy, O Procopius, and didst exalt the honourable Church, going forward in faith and enlightening us.
